title: Hook Shot Both Hands
description: Post players learn the jump hook with either hand from the block, shielding the ball with the body and the off arm.

content.objective: Shoot a jump hook with the right and left hand, keeping the body between the defender and the ball.
content.setup: Player on the right block with a ball, back to the baseline-side sideline.
content.organization: Individual or pairs (one rebounds and passes).
instructions: Start on the right block facing the sideline, ball under the chin.
Drop-step toward the middle with the left foot and turn the shoulders square to the sideline.
Lift the ball with the right hand past the ear, off arm up as a shield.
Release at the top with a wrist flick over the head; land on both feet.
Repeat from the left block with the left hand.
coachingPoints: Shoulders stay perpendicular to the baseline.
commonMistakes: Turning to face the rim (it becomes a fade).
Pushing off with the off arm.
Releasing low in front of the face.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
progressions: Add a defender with a pad.
Hook from a catch on the move across the lane.
regressions: Stand one step closer to the rim.
successCriteria: Six of ten made with each hand.
No offensive fouls with the off arm.
content.gameApplication: The hook is the hardest post shot to block because the body is between the defender and the ball.
